entries.weakness: METRIC CHANGE (not a harness change). Per-run `accuracy` was Bernoulli: hidden-checks were fail-fast and rw-9's llm-judge rubric literally instructed a binary verdict ("Score 1.0 if ... Score 0.0 if ..."). Measured rw-9: [0,1,0,1,1,0,1,0,1,0], p=0.50, sd=0.50. At that spread the gate's own runsNeeded puts a 3pp lift at ~556 runs/arm (20,016 cells per full ablation). The project's 3pp lift rule was UNMEASURABLE, not unmet -- which is why this ledger has zero `adopted` entries.
entries.hypothesis: Grading the SAME checks (n assertions -> pass/total) moves accuracy off the Bernoulli endpoints and collapses its variance, without weakening what is asked of the agent. rw-9's expected values are fixed (the mock API and fallback-prices.json serve identical numbers), so its accuracy can be deterministic -- removing LLM-judge sampling noise from the metric entirely. resilience/tool-mastery keep their judge rubrics.
entries.rationale: DECLARED, owner-approved. This entry exists so the metric change is on the record and NOT mistaken for a harness improvement. No lift is claimed. Scope: gradedCheckHarness() (counts assertions instead of exiting on the first failure) applied to rw-4 (5 requirements) and rw-8 (2 halves); rw-9 converted llm-judge -> deterministic graded verifiable (11 checks). Anti-reward-hacking unchanged: hidden-checks are scorer-written fixtures the agent never sees; partial credit rewards partial WORK, not partial guessing. MEASURED effect on rw-9 accuracy, live cogito:8b n=3: per-run [1, 0.4545, 1], sd 0.500 -> 0.257 (the 0.4545 run scored 0.0 under the old scorer). runs/arm to resolve 3pp: 556 -> 147 (3.8x cheaper). The 3pp threshold itself was NOT changed -- lowering the bar to fit the noise would be gaming it. Comparability: results scored before 2026-07-09 are NOT comparable on `accuracy` for rw-4/rw-8/rw-9. rw-1 and rw-2 remain llm-judge (not deterministically checkable) and remain Bernoulli.

entries.weakness: Agent-execution timeout/crash cells (run.status==='error', scoreErrorCell in packages/benchmarks/src/judge.ts:345-353) are scored as a confident, aggregatable accuracy=0 instead of scoreState:'inconclusive' -- the exact same class of confound cc015306 (2026-07-26, same-day) just fixed for judge-server outages, left open for the sibling agent-timeout path. isRunInconclusive/measuredRuns (report-format.ts:60-79) key ONLY on the judge's scoreState field, which scoreErrorCell never sets, so a cell that never produced output (real GPU/ollama contention forced 2 of 2 independent live single-model qwen3:4b/rw-2/ra-full runs to hit exactly the 150s timeoutMs ceiling) is folded into solveRate/lift-gate math as if the model tried and failed, with session-level partialMeasurement:false and inconclusiveCells:[] giving zero downstream visibility that these are infra timeouts.
entries.hypothesis: Stamp scoreErrorCell's dimensions with scoreState:'inconclusive', inconclusiveReason:'execution-timeout' (mirroring the BenchDimensionScore shape the judge-outage lane already uses) so the existing isRunInconclusive/measuredRuns/isCellInconclusive machinery (already generically keyed on scoreState, needs zero new plumbing) picks it up for free; a domain warden (reasoning/kernel or benchmarks owner) should verify TaskVariantReport.inconclusive / session partialMeasurement also flip when 100% of a cell's runs are execution-errors.
entries.rationale: UNDERPOWERED · 1 tier(s) · 0.0pp lift · -100.0% tok — too few runs to resolve ≥3pp; this is NOT evidence of no effect
